### `todo_app_todo_histories`

Main history table that records each edit operation performed on todos
with timestamp and user context. This table serves as the primary audit
trail for todo modifications, capturing when changes were made and by
whom. Each entry represents a distinct edit event that may involve
changes to title, description, start date, or due date fields. The
history entries are immutable once created and provide comprehensive
tracking for compliance and user transparency.

This table works in conjunction with child tables that track individual
field changes, ensuring proper normalization and granular audit
capabilities. Users can view complete edit histories for each todo,
including who made changes and when specific fields were modified.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_todo_id`: Reference to the todo being edited. [todo_app_todos.id](#todo_app_todos)
- `todo_app_user_id`: Reference to the user who performed the edit. [todo_app_users.id](#todo_app_users)
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the history entry was created. Records when the edit
  > operation occurred.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the history entry was last updated. Typically matches
  > created_at since history entries are immutable.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the history entry was soft deleted. Used for audit trail
  > preservation while supporting cleanup operations.

### `todo_app_todo_history_changes`

Field-level change tracking that records specific field modifications
within each history entry.

This table captures individual field changes that occur during todo
edits, providing granular audit trail capabilities. Each record
represents a single field modification within a broader edit operation
recorded in [todo_app_todo_histories](#todo_app_todo_histories). The table supports tracking
changes to title, description, start date, and due date fields with both
previous and new values stored for complete change history.

The design ensures comprehensive audit capabilities while maintaining
data integrity through proper foreign key relationships and indexing
strategies.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_todo_history_id`: Parent history entry reference. [todo_app_todo_histories.id](#todo_app_todo_histories)
- `field_name`
  > Name of the field that was modified (title, description, start_date,
  > due_date).
- `previous_value`: Value of the field before the edit operation.
- `new_value`: Value of the field after the edit operation.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this field change was recorded.

### `todo_app_todo_history_snapshots`

Tracks the creation of history snapshots for audit trail purposes. This
table records when snapshots are generated from todo history entries,
serving as metadata for the snapshot creation process rather than storing
the actual snapshot data.

Each entry represents a snapshot generation event, linking back to the
specific history entry that triggered the snapshot creation. This table
works in conjunction with [todo_app_todo_histories](#todo_app_todo_histories) to track
snapshot operations and with the actual snapshot storage tables for
complete audit trail functionality.

The primary purpose is to maintain an audit trail of when snapshots were
created, allowing the system to track snapshot generation patterns and
manage snapshot lifecycle operations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_todo_history_id`
  > Reference to the history entry that triggered this snapshot creation.
  > [todo_app_todo_histories.id](#todo_app_todo_histories)
- `snapshot_created_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot event was recorded, representing when the
  > snapshot generation occurred.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot event record was created in the database.

### `todo_app_history_metadata`

System metadata table for history tracking configuration and cleanup
management.

This table stores configuration settings, cleanup policies, retention
periods, and operational metadata for the history tracking system. It
supports the main history tables by providing system-level configuration
and management capabilities.

The metadata includes settings for automatic cleanup operations,
retention policies for historical data, and configuration parameters that
control how the history system operates. This ensures consistent behavior
across the history tracking functionality and provides audit trails for
system operations.

[todo_app_todo_histories](#todo_app_todo_histories) and other history tables reference these
configuration settings to determine retention periods and cleanup
behavior.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `config_key`: Unique key identifier for the configuration setting.
- `config_value`: Value of the configuration setting.
- `config_description`: Description of what this configuration setting controls.
- `is_active`: Whether this configuration setting is currently active.
- `retention_days`: Number of days to retain history data before automatic cleanup.
- `cleanup_frequency`: Frequency of automatic cleanup operations (daily, weekly, monthly).
- `max_history_entries`: Maximum number of history entries to retain per todo item.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this configuration was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this configuration was last updated.

### `todo_app_todo_history_snapshot_items`

Stores denormalized point-in-time snapshots of todo states for
comprehensive audit trail purposes.

This table captures the complete state of todos at specific edit moments,
including all fields (title, description, start date, due date,
completion status) in a denormalized format optimized for audit trail
queries. Each snapshot item represents the state of a todo at a specific
point in time, allowing for complete historical reconstruction and audit
trail functionality.

The denormalized structure ensures that audit trail queries can retrieve
complete todo states without requiring complex joins across multiple
tables, making historical analysis and recovery operations more
efficient. [todo_app_todo_history_snapshots](#todo_app_todo_history_snapshots) provides the parent
snapshot context for each set of snapshot items.

This table is essential for supporting edit history viewing, undo
operations, and compliance requirements where complete historical state
information is necessary.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_todo_history_snapshot_id`
  > Parent snapshot that this item belongs to. {@link
  > todo_app_todo_history_snapshots.id}
- `todo_app_todo_id`: The todo that this snapshot item represents. [todo_app_todos.id](#todo_app_todos)
- `title`: The title of the todo at the time of the snapshot.
- `description`
  > The description of the todo at the time of the snapshot. Can be empty if
  > no description was set.
- `start_date`
  > The start date of the todo at the time of the snapshot. Null if no start
  > date was set.
- `due_date`
  > The due date of the todo at the time of the snapshot. Null if no due date
  > was set.
- `is_completed`: Whether the todo was completed at the time of the snapshot.

### `todo_app_todo_history_snapshot_metadata`

Metadata table for tracking snapshot generation details and audit trail
information.

This table stores metadata specifically related to todo history snapshot
operations, including generation timing, system context, and audit trail
information. It provides supplemental data for the snapshot generation
process that doesn't belong in the main snapshot table.

Each metadata record is associated with a specific snapshot generation
event and contains technical details about the generation process that
support audit requirements and system monitoring. This metadata supports
compliance requirements and provides visibility into snapshot operations
without duplicating parent table attributes.

[todo_app_todo_history_snapshots](#todo_app_todo_history_snapshots) records reference this metadata
for comprehensive audit trail support.

Properties as follows:

- `todo_app_todo_history_snapshot_id`

  > todo_app_todo_history_snapshots.id}
- `generation_duration_ms`: Duration of the snapshot generation process in milliseconds.
- `snapshot_size_bytes`: Size of the generated snapshot data in bytes.
- `system_context`: System context information at the time of snapshot generation.
- `audit_trail_hash`: Hash of the audit trail data for integrity verification.
- `metadata_version`: Version identifier for the metadata schema format.

### `todo_app_trash_items`

Tracks soft-deleted todos and their trash metadata including deletion
timestamp and restoration status. Each entry represents a todo that has
been moved to trash but can potentially be restored. This table maintains
the connection between the deleted todo and its original owner while
tracking the deletion event.

When a user deletes a todo, a record is created here to track the
deletion. If the todo is restored, the restoration status is updated. If
permanently deleted, the record remains for audit purposes but the todo
reference is cleared.

This table supports the trash management workflow by providing the
necessary metadata for restoration operations and trash cleanup
processes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_user_id`: User who owns this trash item. [todo_app_users.id](#todo_app_users)
- `todo_app_todo_id`: Soft-deleted todo reference. [todo_app_todos.id](#todo_app_todos)
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the todo was moved to trash.
- `restored_at`: Timestamp when the todo was restored from trash. Null if still in trash.
- `permanently_deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was permanently deleted from trash. Null if not
  > permanently deleted.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this trash item record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this trash item record was last updated.

### `todo_app_trash_restorations`

Records restoration events when users restore deleted todos from trash
back to active status.

Each restoration event captures when a user restores a previously deleted
todo back to active status, creating an audit trail for accidental
deletion recovery operations. The table maintains references to both the
user who performed the restoration and the specific trash item that was
restored.

This table supports the application's safety features by providing
complete visibility into restoration operations, enabling users to track
their recovery actions and providing data isolation guarantees that
ensure users can only access restoration events for their own todos.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_trash_item_id`
  > Reference to the trash item being restored. {@link
  > todo_app_trash_items.id}
- `todo_app_user_id`
  > Reference to the user who performed the restoration. {@link
  > todo_app_users.id}
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the restoration event was created and recorded.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the restoration record was last updated (typically matches
  > created_at for restoration events).

### `todo_app_permanent_deletions`

Tracks permanent deletion operations for audit purposes and compliance
requirements.

This table serves as an audit trail for when users permanently delete
todos from the trash system. Each record captures who deleted what todo
and when, providing comprehensive audit capabilities for compliance and
user accountability.

Records in this table are append-only and represent the final step in the
todo lifecycle when items are removed from the trash. The table
references [todo_app_users.id](#todo_app_users) for user accountability and {@link
todo_app_todos.id} for tracking which todo was permanently deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_user_id`
  > Reference to the user who performed the permanent deletion. {@link
  > todo_app_users.id}
- `todo_app_todo_id`
  > Reference to the todo that was permanently deleted. {@link
  > todo_app_todos.id}
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the permanent deletion occurred.
- `reason`: Optional reason for permanent deletion, if provided by the user.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp for audit trail.
- `updated_at`: Record update timestamp for audit trail.

### `todo_app_trash_cleanup_logs`

Logs automated trash cleanup operations and system-initiated permanent
deletions for audit and monitoring purposes.

This table records all system-generated cleanup activities that
permanently remove expired items from the trash. Each entry tracks
operation details including processed item counts, success/failure
status, cleanup criteria, and performance metrics. These logs provide
audit trails for compliance requirements and system monitoring.

Relationship context: References [todo_app_trash_items](#todo_app_trash_items) to track
which items were processed in each cleanup operation. Connected to system
metadata through cleanup criteria references.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_trash_item_id`
  > References the specific trash item processed in this cleanup operation.
  > [todo_app_trash_items.id](#todo_app_trash_items)
- `operation_type`
  > Type of cleanup operation performed (e.g., 'automatic_cleanup',
  > 'manual_cleanup', 'expired_item_removal').
- `items_processed`: Number of trash items processed in this cleanup operation.
- `items_deleted`: Number of items permanently deleted during this cleanup.
- `cleanup_criteria`: Criteria used to select items for cleanup (e.g., 'older_than_30_days').
- `operation_status`
  > Status of the cleanup operation (e.g., 'completed', 'failed',
  > 'partial_success').
- `error_message`: Error details if the cleanup operation failed.
- `started_at`: Timestamp when the cleanup operation began.
- `completed_at`: Timestamp when the cleanup operation finished.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.

### `todo_app_trash_settings`

Stores user preferences for trash retention periods and cleanup
automation settings.

Each user can configure personal preferences for how their deleted todos
are managed in the trash system. This includes automatic cleanup
timeframes, notification preferences, and retention policies that
determine when items are permanently deleted from the trash.

The settings support flexible trash management while ensuring user
control over data retention and cleanup automation. All settings default
to system-wide values but can be customized per user to accommodate
different workflow preferences.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_user_id`: Associated user's [todo_app_users.id](#todo_app_users) who owns these trash settings.
- `retention_period_days`
  > Number of days to keep items in trash before automatic cleanup. Default
  > system value is 30 days.
- `auto_cleanup_enabled`: Whether automatic cleanup of expired trash items is enabled for this user.
- `notify_before_cleanup`
  > Whether to send notifications before items are automatically cleaned up
  > from trash.
- `notify_days_before`
  > Number of days before cleanup to send notification. Only relevant if
  > notify_before_cleanup is true.
- `permanent_deletion_confirmation`
  > Whether to require confirmation before permanently deleting items from
  > trash.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when these trash settings were created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when these trash settings were last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when these trash settings were soft deleted (if applicable).

### `todo_app_trash_item_metadata`

Tracks supplemental metadata for trash items to support automated cleanup
processes and retention management.

This table stores additional information needed for the trash management
system beyond basic deletion tracking. It enables features like automated
cleanup eligibility determination, retention period enforcement, and
cleanup status tracking. The metadata supports compliance requirements
and user configurable retention preferences.

Each record represents the cleanup and retention configuration for a
single trash item from [todo_app_trash_items](#todo_app_trash_items). The table maintains
critical timing information for automated cleanup decisions and provides
status tracking for retention policy enforcement.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_trash_item_id`: Reference to the trash item being tracked. [todo_app_trash_items.id](#todo_app_trash_items)
- `cleanup_eligible`
  > Indicates if this trash item is eligible for automated cleanup based on
  > retention policies.
- `retention_expires_at`
  > Calculated timestamp when retention period expires and automated cleanup
  > can occur.
- `cleanup_scheduled_at`: Timestamp when automated cleanup is scheduled to process this trash item.
- `manual_cleanup_requested`
  > Flag indicating if user explicitly requested cleanup bypassing retention
  > period.
- `cleanup_processed_at`: Timestamp when automated cleanup was successfully processed.

text: I'll execute the Interface Agent to create the API interface specification based on our database schema and requirements.

instruction:
Create API interfaces for a multi-user Todo application with the following functionality:

## User Authentication
- User sign up with email and password
- User login with email and password
- Password change functionality
- Account deletion (with cleanup of all user data)

## User Profile Management
- Get user profile
- Update display name

## Todo CRUD Operations
- Create todo (title, description, start_date, due_date)
- Get paginated todo list (with filtering by completion status)
- Get single todo with full details
- Update todo (title, description, start_date, due_date)
- Soft delete todo
- Toggle todo completion status

## Todo Filtering and Sorting
- Filter by: all/complete/incomplete
- Sort by: creation date, start date, due date (asc/desc)
- Handle null dates appropriately in sorting

## Edit History
- Get todo edit history (paginated, newest first)
- Each history entry shows what fields changed and when

## Trash Management
- Get paginated trash list
- Restore todo from trash
- Permanently delete todo from trash (cascading delete history)

## Privacy Requirements
- All operations must be user-scoped (users only access their own data)
- No cross-user data access allowed

operations.specification:
The join operation creates a new user account by validating the email uniqueness and password strength, then storing the hashed password in the database. It generates JWT tokens for immediate authentication after registration.

The implementation should:
1. Validate email format and check uniqueness against existing users
2. Validate password meets security requirements
3. Hash the password using bcrypt with appropriate salt rounds
4. Create user record with email, hashed password, and display name
5. Generate access and refresh tokens with user claims
6. Return tokens in the authorized response

Business rules from requirements:
- Email must be unique across all users
- Password must meet security requirements
- Display name is required
- Account creation timestamp is recorded

Error handling:
- Return specific validation errors for email/password issues
- Handle database constraints for duplicate emails
- Ensure secure token generation
operations.description:
User registration endpoint that creates a new account with email and password authentication.

This operation allows new users to register for the Todo application by providing their email address, password, and display name. The system validates the email format, ensures email uniqueness across all users, and validates password strength according to security requirements. Upon successful validation, the user account is created with the provided credentials and profile information.

The operation generates both access and refresh JWT tokens upon successful registration, allowing the user to immediately authenticate and begin using the application. The access token has a 30-minute expiration while the refresh token lasts for 30 days, following the security specifications outlined in the authentication requirements.

Security considerations include proper password hashing using industry-standard algorithms, email validation to prevent abuse, and secure token generation with appropriate claims including user ID and role information. The system maintains complete data isolation between users, ensuring privacy guarantees from the moment of account creation.

Related operations include the login endpoint for existing users and the refresh endpoint for token renewal. This registration workflow is the entry point for new users to access the Todo application's personal task management capabilities.

requestBody.description: Registration information including email, password, and display name

responseBody.description: JWT tokens for immediate authentication after successful registration

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
The login operation authenticates existing users by validating email and password credentials against stored hashed passwords.

The implementation should:
1. Find user by email (case-insensitive lookup)
2. Verify password hash matches using bcrypt compare
3. Generate new access and refresh tokens
4. Update last login timestamp if needed
5. Return tokens in authorized response

Business rules from requirements:
- Invalid credentials return generic error (don't specify email/password)
- Implement rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks
- Follow secure token generation practices

Error handling:
- Handle invalid credentials with generic error message
- Account lockout after excessive failed attempts
- Token generation failures
operations.description:
User authentication endpoint that validates email and password credentials for existing users.

This operation allows registered users to authenticate and obtain JWT tokens for accessing the Todo application. The system validates the provided email and password against stored credentials, ensuring secure authentication through proper password hashing comparison. Upon successful validation, the operation generates new access and refresh tokens with appropriate expiration times.

The authentication process follows industry security standards by using bcrypt for password comparison, implementing rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks, and providing generic error messages that don't reveal whether the email or password was incorrect. This bulk operation provides significant efficiency improvements over individual restoration operations when users need to recover multiple accidentally deleted todos.

Check that none of the specified todos have been permanently deleted (permanently_deleted_at is null). For each valid todo, update the todo_app_todos.deleted_at field to null to mark as active, create a restoration record in todo_app_trash_restorations, and update the todo_app_trash_items.restored_at timestamp. Use database transactions to ensure atomicity - if any restoration fails, rollback all changes. Return a paginated summary of the restored todos with basic information for confirmation. Handle validation errors gracefully with appropriate error messages.

operations.specification: Process bulk permanent deletion of todos from trash. Validate that all provided todo IDs belong to the authenticated user and exist in the trash (not already restored or permanently deleted). Perform cascading deletion of all related records including todo_histories, todo_completions, and trash_items. Use transaction to ensure atomicity - if any todo fails validation or deletion, rollback the entire operation. Return detailed summary of successful and failed deletions with error reasons for failures.
operations.description:
Permanently delete multiple todos from the trash in a single operation.

This bulk operation allows users to efficiently remove multiple soft-deleted todos from the system permanently. The operation validates that all specified todos belong to the requesting user and are currently in the trash (not restored or already permanently deleted).

When successful, the operation performs cascading deletion of all related records including edit history entries, completion status changes, and trash metadata. The deletion is atomic - if any individual todo fails validation or deletion, the entire operation is rolled back to maintain data consistency.

The response provides a detailed summary including the number of successfully deleted todos and any failures with specific error messages. This allows users to understand the outcome of the bulk operation and take appropriate action for any items that could not be deleted.

This operation is part of the comprehensive trash management system that supports the soft deletion workflow, enabling users to recover accidentally deleted todos while providing a mechanism for permanent cleanup when needed.

operations.specification:
Implement a comprehensive search operation that queries the todo_app_todos table with advanced filtering and sorting capabilities.

Query Strategy:
- Join with todo_app_todo_description_fields for text search in descriptions
- Join with todo_app_todo_completions for completion status filtering
- Support partial text matching on todo titles using trigram indexing
- Implement pagination with cursor-based or offset-based approach
- Apply user ownership filtering to ensure data isolation

Search Features:
- Text search across title and description fields
- Filter by completion status (all/complete/incomplete)
- Sort by creation date, start date, due date with direction
- Handle null dates appropriately in sorting
- Return summary information optimized for search results

Performance Considerations:
- Use database indexes on title (gin_trgm_ops) and description
- Implement efficient joins with proper indexing
- Consider search result caching for repeated queries
- Optimize pagination for large result sets
operations.description:
Perform a comprehensive search across the user's todo items with advanced filtering, sorting, and text matching capabilities.

This operation allows authenticated users to search through their personal todo collection using various criteria including text content, completion status, and date ranges. The search spans across todo titles and optional description fields, providing flexible search capabilities for efficient todo management.

The search supports partial text matching using trigram indexing for fuzzy search functionality. Users can filter results by completion status to focus on active tasks or review completed items. Advanced sorting options allow organizing results by creation date, start date, or due date in ascending or descending order.

Results are returned in paginated format with summary information optimized for search result displays. Each result includes essential todo information while maintaining efficient query performance even with large todo collections.

Security and privacy are maintained through strict user ownership validation, ensuring that users can only search through their own todo data. The operation integrates with the application's comprehensive privacy framework to prevent any cross-user data access.

This search functionality complements the standard todo list operations by providing targeted search capabilities for users with large todo collections or specific search requirements.

text: I'll execute the Test Agent to create comprehensive E2E test suites for our Todo application API interfaces

instruction:
Create E2E tests for a multi-user Todo API with the following test scenarios:

## User Authentication Tests
- User registration with valid and invalid data
- User login with correct and incorrect credentials
- Password change functionality
- Account deletion and data cleanup

## User Profile Tests
- Get user profile
- Update display name

## Todo CRUD Tests
- Create todo with various field combinations
- Get paginated todo list with different filters and sorts
- Get single todo details
- Update todo fields individually and in combination
- Soft delete and restore operations
- Toggle todo completion status

## Edit History Tests
- Verify history entries are created on todo edits
- Get todo edit history pagination
- History accuracy for field changes

## Trash Management Tests
- View trash list
- Restore deleted todos
- Permanent deletion with history cleanup

## Privacy and Security Tests
- User isolation (users cannot access other users' data)
- Authorization checks for all endpoints
- Data validation and error handling

## Integration Tests
- Complete workflow: register → login → create todos → edit → delete → restore
- Multiple users operating independently
- Data persistence and consistency

scenario.draft:
Test the complete user workflow of setting up personalized trash management preferences. As a registered user authenticated with valid JWT tokens, configure a comprehensive set of trash settings that align with business rules. Validate that the system correctly processes all configurable fields: retention_period_days (set to 30 days within the 1-365 range), auto_cleanup_enabled (true), notify_before_cleanup (true), notify_days_before (7 days which is less than retention_period_days), and permanent_deletion_confirmation (true). Verify that the response contains the complete updated ITodoAppTrashSetting object with all fields populated, including system-generated IDs and timestamps. Confirm the updated_at timestamp reflects the current update time. Test idempotency by sending the identical request again and verifying the response remains unchanged.

Business logic validations to check: ensure notify_days_before (7) is less than retention_period_days (30) when notify_before_cleanup is enabled, ensure retention_period_days is within the 1-365 day range, verify that the settings are completely isolated to the authenticated user only. After successful update, validate the system behavior by checking that subsequent trash management operations (like viewing trash items) respect these configured settings.

Edge cases to consider: verify that partial updates work where only a subset of fields are provided in subsequent requests, test that retention_period_days boundary values (1 and 365) are accepted, confirm that authentication is required and unauthorized requests are rejected.

scenario.draft:
Test that the update operation supports partial field updates while preserving existing values for omitted fields. Authenticate as a user, then perform a partial update request where only retention_period_days and permanent_deletion_confirmation are provided, while leaving auto_cleanup_enabled, notify_before_cleanup, and notify_days_before fields unchanged. Verify that the response includes all settings fields, with the explicitly provided fields updated to the new values, and the omitted fields retaining their previous values from the database. This tests the partial update capability of the IUpdate DTO where all fields are optional.

Key business logic validation: ensure that when notify_before_cleanup is left enabled from previous configuration but notify_days_before is not provided in the partial update, the system should preserve the existing notify_days_before value and not trigger false validation errors. Similarly, when retention_period_days is updated to a new value, ensure that if notify_before_cleanup is enabled and notify_days_before is not provided, the preserved notify_days_before value still satisfies the business rule that notify_days_before must be less than retention_period_days (if not, this should trigger a validation error).

Also test idempotent partial updates: sending the same partial update request multiple times should produce identical results. Validate that timestamps (created_at and updated_at) are handled correctly - created_at should remain unchanged, updated_at should reflect the most recent modification time.

dependencies.purpose: Authentication as user - the trash settings update endpoint requires an authenticated user context and authorizationActor 'user'. This provides the necessary JWT tokens.

scenario.draft:
Test the business logic validation rules around notification settings that involve cross-field dependencies. Authenticate as a user and attempt to update trash settings with notify_before_cleanup enabled but notify_days_before equal to or greater than retention_period_days. According to the specifications, this should trigger a business logic validation error (not a simple HTTP 400 validation error) because notify_days_before must be less than retention_period_days when notifications are enabled.

Test scenarios: (1) retention_period_days = 30, notify_before_cleanup = true, notify_days_before = 30 (equal) - should fail, (2) retention_period_days = 30, notify_before_cleanup = true, notify_days_before = 31 (greater) - should fail, (3) retention_period_days = 30, notify_before_cleanup = true, notify_days_before = 29 (valid) - should succeed, (4) notify_before_cleanup = false, notify_days_before = any value (including invalid ones) - should succeed because notification validation only applies when notifications are enabled.

Important: This tests business logic validation, not simple HTTP validation. The system should check the relationship between these fields when notify_before_cleanup is true and return an appropriate business rule violation error message that explains the constraint. Confirm that the error response distinguishes this from simple schema validation failures.

text: I'll execute the Realize Agent to implement the actual business logic for all the API endpoints in our Todo application.

instruction:
Implement business logic for a multi-user Todo API with the following functionality:

## User Authentication Implementation
- User registration with email/password validation and hashing
- JWT-based authentication for login
- Password change with proper security measures
- Account deletion with complete data cleanup (cascading delete todos, edit history, trash items)

## User Profile Implementation
- Profile retrieval with JWT authorization
- Display name update with validation

## Todo Business Logic
- Create todo with default completion status (incomplete)
- Get paginated todo list with filtering by completion status
- Get single todo with authorization check
- Update todo with automatic edit history creation
- Soft delete implementation (mark as deleted without physical removal)
- Completion status toggle

## Filtering and Sorting Logic
- Filter todos by completion status (all/complete/incomplete)
- Sort todos by creation date, start date, due date (asc/desc)
- Handle null dates in sorting (nulls last)

## Edit History Implementation
- Automatic audit trail on todo updates
- Record changed fields only (don't record unchanged fields)
- Paginated history retrieval

## Trash Management Implementation
- Separate trash view with pagination
- Restore functionality (reverse soft delete)
- Permanent deletion with cascading history removal

## Security and Privacy
- User-level data isolation (users only access their own data)
- Authorization middleware for all endpoints
- Input validation and sanitization
- Error handling for authorization failures

authorizations.error_analysis:
The primary compilation error is in src/MyGlobal.ts at position 279-298: 'Cannot find module './MyConfiguration' or its corresponding type declarations.'

This is a critical path resolution issue where the MyGlobal module imports a configuration file that doesn't exist or is in the wrong location. The MyGlobal module is imported by the userAuthorize provider, so this error would propagate through the entire authentication system, causing all components to fail compilation.

While the authorization components themselves (userAuthorize, UserAuth, UserPayload) appear syntactically correct, they cannot compile because their dependency (MyGlobal) has a fatal import error. The table name 'todo_app_users' in the userAuthorize function also needs to be verified against the actual database schema.
authorizations.solution_guidance:
1. Fix the MyGlobal.ts import error:
   - Check if the MyConfiguration.ts file exists in the same directory as MyGlobal.ts
   - If it doesn't exist, either create it or adjust the import path
   - The import should be: import * as MyConfiguration from './MyConfiguration' (or adjust path)

2. Verify database table name:
   - The query uses 'todo_app_users.findFirst()' which needs to match the actual Prisma model name
   - If the schema uses 'user' instead of 'todo_app_users', update the query accordingly

3. Ensure all imports are correct:
   - userAuthorize imports jwtAuthorize from './jwtAuthorize' (same directory)
   - userAuthorize imports UserPayload from '../../decorators/payload/UserPayload'
   - Decorator imports userAuthorize from '../providers/authorize/userAuthorize'

4. Test compilation after fixing the MyGlobal.ts import issue

plan.thinking: ITodoAppTodo.ICreate is a collectable DTO that maps to todo_app_todos table. It creates new todo records with title provided by user and user_id from authenticated actor.

This DTO maps to todo_app_todo_histories table with computed fields for operation_type. It's a read DTO used for activity timeline display with direct database table mapping. Transformable because it represents aggregated historical operations from database queries.

Transforms todo_app_todo_histories table with joined user and todo summaries. ISummary DTO is a read DTO used for API responses, maps directly to database table with x-autobe-database-schema annotation, and contains database-backed fields with JOINs to related tables. Transformable as it converts todo_app_todo_histories with nested user and todo summaries.
Direct mapping to todo_app_todo_history_changes table. Contains field change records with timestamps and history relations. Used for API responses to show field change details. Transformable.
Summary DTO maps directly to todo_app_todo_history_snapshots table with id, snapshot_created_at, and created_at fields. Used for API responses reading from database, meets all transformable criteria.

ITodoAppUser is a Read DTO used for API responses that maps directly to todo_app_users database table. It contains all public user fields (id, email, display_name, timestamps) and excludes sensitive password_hash. This is a transformable DTO that requires a transformer to convert database records to API responses.

ITodoAppTrashCleanupLog.ISummary is a read DTO (Summary variant) that maps directly to database table 'todo_app_trash_cleanup_logs'. All properties reference database fields with x-autobe-database-schema-property annotations. This is a database-backed entity response DTO that needs a transformer to convert from database model to API response format.

ITodoAppTodoHistory is a Read DTO used for API responses that maps directly to the todo_app_todo_histories database table. It contains core fields from the history table and includes relations to todo and user summaries, making it transformable.

ITodoAppTodoCompletion is a Read DTO used for API responses. It has x-autobe-database-schema annotation mapping to todo_app_todo_completions table. All fields directly map to database columns: id, completed, created_at. The DTO is DB-backed and used for GET operations. Transformable.

ITodoAppTrashItem is a transformable DTO that maps to todo_app_trash_items table. It contains database timestamp fields and embedded relationships to user and todo summaries via foreign keys. This DTO is used for API responses to display trash management data.
Transforms todo_app_trash_items to ITodoAppTrashItem.ISummary with core trash metadata fields and embedded todo summary relation for display purposes

This DTO maps to todo_app_trash_cleanup_logs table as it's a complete audit trail recording automated cleanup operations with direct field mappings and database schema reference. Contains operation details, statistics, and timing information for audit purposes.

ITodoAppUser.ISummary is a read DTO that maps directly to the todo_app_users database table. Contains essential user fields like id, email, display_name, and created_at for summary display purposes. Transformable because it's a DB-backed response DTO used for API responses.

ITodoAppTodo.ISummary is a Read DTO that maps directly to the todo_app_todos table. The x-autobe-database-schema extension confirms this direct mapping. It contains essential fields for list displays and is database-backed, making it transformable.

ITodoAppTrashSetting maps to todo_app_trash_settings table with direct field mapping. It has x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirming transformability. This is a read DTO for user trash settings configuration.

Complete todo entity with direct mapping from todo_app_todos table. Includes core fields (id, title, timestamps) and joined user summary. Has x-autobe-database-schema property indicating table mapping, so transformer needed.
Transforms todo_app_permanent_deletions table with user and todo relation mappings for audit trail purposes

This DTO maps to todo_app_todo_history_snapshot_items table. It is a read DTO for API responses containing historical snapshot data. The interface schema shows direct field mappings (title, description, start_date, due_date, is_completed → completed_at) with x-autobe-database-schema property confirming the table mapping. It meets all transformable criteria: read DTO, DB-backed, direct mapping to primary database table.

ITodoAppAuditLog maps directly to todo_app_audit_logs table. It's a Read DTO used for API responses, database-backed, and has direct mapping to a primary database table. Therefore, it is transformable.

Summary DTO maps directly to todo_app_todo_history_snapshot_items table for audit trail display. Contains snapshot item data with timestamp metadata from related snapshot. Transformable as it's a read DTO for API responses that directly corresponds to database table structure.
Transforms todo_app_history_metadata table configuration data to ITodoAppHistoryMetadatum DTO with all fields mapped including configuration settings, retention policies, and timestamps

This DTO has x-autobe-database-schema property explicitly set to 'todo_app_history_metadata' and maps directly to database fields. It is a read DTO used for API responses that comes from database queries, making it transformable.

ITodoAppTrashItemMetadatum is a Read DTO that maps directly to todo_app_trash_item_metadata table. It contains database-backed fields with direct column mappings, making it transformable for API response generation.
